OOS_protocol.data_window: to be fixed in the registration before any data is read
OOS_protocol.train_test_boundary: universe membership frozen as of each fold's train end; cohort definitions fixed before any holding window is read

capacity_model.note: set by the thinnest leg's depth; not measured in this repo

counterparty: leveraged longs in high-funding perps (pay) and shorts in low-funding perps (pay), within the same funding-interval cohort
drawdown_model: measured on price+funding P&L of the dollar-neutral perp book; funding-only drawdown is not a drawdown
economic_mechanism: Counterparty: leveraged longs in the high-funding perp pay; shorts in the low/negative-funding perp pay. Hypothesis: the 'funding level predicts the next funding' relation differs by funding-interval cohort (480m / 240m / 60m) because shorter intervals re-price the premium more often and are capped per print differently, so ranking WITHIN a cohort (on interval-normalised bps/day) predicts the holding-window funding better than ranking across cohorts, which mixes a mechanical interval artefact with the economic signal. Persists while the cohorts keep different re-pricing cadence; vanishes if the cross-cohort ranking is just as predictive, if cohorts are too thin, or when the high-funding names are delisted or squeezed (a perp-only spread is NOT a carry: price legs are the risk).
eligibility_rules: symbol active at decision time per the PIT universe (verified universe_capture, Closed contracts included)
funding interval is per symbol as the venue states it; ranking uses interval-normalised bps/day within the cohort
minimum 30d listing age and a stated minimum open interest
a cohort with fewer than 2 x top_k eligible symbols at a decision produces no row
entry: at each rebalance on the fixed non-overlapping grid, within each cohort short the top-k and long the bottom-k by trailing interval-normalised funding, dollar-neutral
execution_model: taker both legs, perp only; price-leg residual and beta to the equal-weight universe measured, not assumed away
exit: next rebalance or delivery of a leg

taker_bps.note: carry_costs.TAKER_BPS_PERP: the PERP leg's base-tier taker fee (published schedule); the spot leg is spot_taker_bps. A spot+perp round trip is 2 x (taker_bps + spot_taker_bps) = 31.0 bps

funding_interval_handling.method: interval-normalised: funding_bps_per_day = rate_bps * 1440 / fundingInterval_min per symbol; holding-horizon funding = bps/day x days; per-interval cohorts (480m / 240m / 60m) reported separately; settlement grid is per symbol; a Closed contract earns nothing after its deliveryTime
funding_interval_handling.source_of_interval_facts: OWNER-OBSERVED live probe (unverified in this repo): Bybit funding interval is per symbol (480m, 240m, sometimes 60m) and 14 of the top 20 positive-funding perps over $5M turnover were 240m contracts
funding_interval_handling.unknown_interval: funding normalisation UNKNOWN -> the candidate cannot pass

holding_period: 7 days on a fixed non-overlapping grid (hold grid registered; every cell counts as a tested variant)
hypothesis: Ranking perps by trailing interval-normalised funding within funding-interval cohorts earns a larger net funding spread than ranking across cohorts.

prospective_protocol.description: register thresholds then observe forward basis excursions and fills on testnet mechanics
prospective_protocol.note: floors only: no start date is claimed here; the registration that opens the window sets and seals it

rejection_conditions: adjusted p-value (Holm over every attempted variant) above 0.05 on historical_test or oos_test
within-cohort ranking does not beat cross-cohort ranking by a registered margin
net edge after assumed costs not positive
universe cannot be shown point-in-time (survivors only)
price-leg P&L over the sample is negative or larger in magnitude than the funding spread earned

required_data.name: funding history per symbol with that symbol's own fundingInterval, all listed symbols incl. Closed

depth/spread per symbol for capacity and slippage
